question: What must a Speed Limit sign display, in what increments, and may it be used to show an advisory speed for a roadway condition?
model_answer: Direct Answer: A Speed Limit (R2-1) sign must display the limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or as adopted by the authorized agency based on an engineering study, and the displayed limits must be in multiples of 5 mph. It should NOT be used to show an advisory speed for a roadway condition — that function belongs to an advisory speed plaque mounted below a warning sign. Standards (mandatory): - "The Speed Limit (R2-1) sign (see Figure 2B-3) shall display the limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or as adopted by the authorized agency based on an engineering study. The speed limits displayed shall be in multiples of 5 mph." Guidance (recommended): - Section 2B.21 further provides (visible in the attached page view): "An advisory speed plaque (see Section 2C.59) mounted below a warning sign should be used to warn road users of an advisory speed for a roadway condition. A Speed Limit sign should not be used for this purpose." Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2B-3 shows the Speed Limit (R2-1) sign displaying "SPEED LIMIT 50" — a limit in a multiple of 5 mph — along with related speed limit signs and plaques. - [Image 2] Shows advisory speeds for a curve conveyed via W13-1P advisory speed plaques mounted with warning signs (not via Speed Limit signs), illustrating the proper device for advisory speeds. - [Image 3] Shows the Section 2B.21 text, including the Standard that the R2-1 sign shall display the established limit in multiples of 5 mph and the Guidance that a Speed Limit sign should not be used to convey an advisory speed for a roadway condition. - [Image 4] Repeats Figure 2B-3, confirming the R2-1 layout and 5-mph-multiple legends (50, 40, 45, 55, etc.). Citations: - Section 2B.21 Standard §13 (p.85) - Figure 2B-3 (p.86) - Page 126 - Page 197
gold_answer: It must display the speed limit established by law, ordinance, regulation, or an authorized agency based on an engineering study, in multiples of 5 mph. It should not be used for an advisory speed; an advisory speed plaque below an appropriate warning sign should be used instead.
